scope: Local zero-credential Mission coordinator leasing and commit-fencing slice
implemented: Versioned .atlas/mission-leases.json state with atomic filesystem updates
Tenant, organisation, project and environment scope binding
Atomic acquire with same-owner renewal and competing-owner conflict
Lease heartbeat with owner and lease identity fencing
Explicit release and expiry transition
Expired lease recovery for a new owner
Coordinator-owned Mission lease around receive, approval, delivery, callback and control operations
Periodic coordinator heartbeat during long operations
Commit-boundary fencing in AtlasLocalRuntime and MissionStore before durable writes
Stale-owner regression proving lease loss rejects before runtime or Mission persistence is written
Lease state is separate from the existing Mission persistence authority and does not create a second Mission execution authority
Scope-local expiry prevents one tenant clock from expiring another tenant's active lease
Takeover is fenced by the Mission lease before runtime or Mission state mutation
Process-level SIGKILL recovery allows a replacement worker to recover an expired lease
Process-level duplicate-worker contention leaves exactly one active lease owner
Process-level Mission workers persist receive, approval, delivery, pause, resume and cancel checkpoints across SIGKILL restart boundaries
An independent dependency-free verifier validates persisted Mission and runtime truth after worker termination, including the no-Action invariant for cancelled Missions
Monotonic release fencing rejects backward-clock cleanup before corrupting persisted lease state
Lease scope validation rejects unexpected persisted properties before acquisition
Lease ownership is checked while holding the lease lock across each guarded durable commit
Stale lock reclamation is serialized with a compare-before-rename reclaim marker

process_worker_tests: two separate worker processes contend for one Mission lease
SIGKILL coordinator after receive, approval and delivery checkpoints
independent verifier reads MissionStore and runtime persisted truth
verification.full_command: cd packages/atlas && npm run metadata:write && npm run metadata:check && npm run build && npx vitest run --testTimeout=30000 && git diff --check

remaining_gate_requirements: Process-kill coverage for every remaining Mission lifecycle/control boundary beyond receive, approval and delivery
A crash matrix covering partial runtime-versus-Mission commits, wait projection, action/outbox commit and callback reconciliation
An independent duplicate-worker commit verifier proving one committed Mission step and one action/outbox/receipt chain
A long-running step heartbeat test across multiple lease TTL intervals followed by owner termination and expiry recovery
Bounded recovery when a live suspended or wedged owner holds the project operation lock beyond Mission lease expiry
verdict: ATLAS-BMR2-P2-001 = IN_PROGRESS / LOCAL_PROVEN: the local lease and checkpoint slices pass, but the literal recovery acceptance remains unproven because crash points do not cover partial lifecycle commits, duplicate-worker step commits, long-step heartbeat behavior, or every remaining lifecycle boundary. CI, database-equivalent persistence, Cloud, provider, staging and production evidence remain absent.
